raw_responses.Bulgarian: DESCRIPTION: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity, with perplexity values plotted on a logarithmic scale on the vertical axis and sparsity rate values ranging from 10% to 80% on the horizontal axis. The horizontal axis is labeled "Sparsity Rate" and displays discrete percentage values at regular intervals. The vertical axis is labeled "Perplexity" and uses a logarithmic scale, with marked values at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. Two data series are represented by colored bars: "Per-Output" in blue and "Per-Layer" in orange. For each sparsity rate, two bars are shown side-by-side, indicating the corresponding perplexity values for each series. The bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate from left to right. The legend in the upper left corner identifies the color coding for the two series. The chart shows that as sparsity rate increases, the perplexity values for both series generally increase, with the "Per-Layer" series consistently exhibiting higher perplexity values than the "Per-Output" series across all sparsity rates.
raw_responses.Chinese: DESCRIPTION: The bar chart compares per-output and per-layer perplexity across different sparsity rates, with the x-axis representing sparsity rate in percentage (10% to 80%) and the y-axis showing perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. Each sparsity rate has two adjacent bars: a blue bar for per-output perplexity and an orange bar for per-layer perplexity. The bars increase in height as sparsity rate increases, with both per-output and per-layer perplexity rising sharply between 70% and 80% sparsity. At 80% sparsity, the per-layer perplexity (orange bar) reaches approximately 10^3, while the per-output perplexity (blue bar) reaches about 10^2.5. The bars for 10% and 20% sparsity are the shortest, with both per-output and per-layer perplexity values around 10^0. The chart is grouped by sparsity rate, with the blue and orange bars side-by-side for each rate, and the groups are ordered in ascending order of sparsity rate.
raw_responses.English: DESCRIPTION: The bar chart illustrates the perplexity values for two different models, "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer," across varying sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, with categories labeled as 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged in ascending order. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 (1) to 10^3 (1000), with major tick marks at 10^0, 10^1, and 10^2. For each sparsity rate, two bars are displayed side-by-side: a blue bar representing "Per-Output" and an orange bar representing "Per-Layer." The height of the bars increases with the sparsity rate for both models. At 10% sparsity, both bars are approximately equal in height, with a perplexity value of around 1. At 80% sparsity, the "Per-Output" bar reaches a perplexity of approximately 500, while the "Per-Layer" bar reaches a value of approximately 1000. The "Per-Layer" model consistently shows higher perplexity than the "Per-Output" model across all sparsity rates. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate, and the legend in the top-left corner identifies the color coding for each model.
